Per-chromosome allelic overdispersion, shrunk to the global

Source: R/caller.R
rho_by_chrom.Rd

The beta-binomial rho of the null allele votes can differ between chromosomes (small chromosomes up to about twice the genome-wide value), so one global rho under-penalises the allelic tails of the more overdispersed ones. Per chromosome, rho is fitted (fit_allelic_null()) on the null rows of classes (default the arms, as the global rho) and shrunk to the global: rho_c = (n x rho_raw + k x rho_global) / (n + k), n = null rows with votes. Chromosomes without null rows (chrX in normal mode) keep the global rho (rho_rows()).

Usage

rho_by_chrom(
  d,
  rho = NULL,
  k = params$rho_chrom_k,
  null = NULL,
  classes = "arm",
  params = caller_defaults()
)

Arguments

d

rows with nA, n_hap, class, chrom (or a parsable region) and a null definition

rho

global rho (NULL: fitted on the same rows)

k

shrinkage pseudo-count (null rows; params$rho_chrom_k)

null

optional logical null flag per row

classes

region classes of the fit

params

caller_defaults()

Value

data.table chrom, n_rows, rho_raw, rho_global, w (= n / (n + k)), rho
